questions.question_text: A triangular frame has sides $9$ m, $12$ m and $15$ m. Find the angle opposite the longest side, and state what kind of triangle this is.

options.why: Put the $12$ m side as $c$ opposite the angle instead of the longest side $15$ m.
Put the $9$ m side as $c$, so found a different angle instead of the one opposite $15$ m.

questions.solution_text:
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}-c^{2}}{2ab}$
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{9^{2}+12^{2}-15^{2}}{2(9)(12)}$
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{0}{216}=0$
$\theta=\cos^{-1}(0)=90^{\circ}$
The angle is exactly $90^{\circ}$, so it is a right-angled triangle.
